requirement.text: The system SHALL reject a medication order when the ordered daily dose of Acetaminophen exceeds the formulary maximum daily dose of 4000 mg defined in the formulary, and SHALL display the formulary maximum daily dose in the rejection message.

test_cases.description: Verify a Acetaminophen order within the formulary maximum daily dose is accepted.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Acetaminophen is 4000 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> Medications and select Acetaminophen.
Step: 2. Enter a regimen totalling 2000 mg per day.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The medication ordering screen is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The daily total of 2000 mg is calculated and shown.
ExpectedResult: 3. The order is accepted and saved, within the formulary maximum daily dose of 4000 mg.

test_cases.description: Verify a Acetaminophen order exceeding the formulary maximum daily dose is rejected.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Acetaminophen is 4000 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> Medications and select Acetaminophen.
Step: 2. Enter a regimen totalling 6000 mg per day.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The medication ordering screen is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The daily total of 6000 mg is calculated and shown.
ExpectedResult: 3. The order is rejected and is not saved.

test_cases.description: Verify the formulary maximum daily dose boundary for Acetaminophen.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Acetaminophen is 4000 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Order Acetaminophen totalling exactly 4000 mg per day and sign.
Step: 2. Order Acetaminophen totalling 4001 mg per day and sign.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At exactly 4000 mg the order is accepted, because the dose did not EXCEED the maximum.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 4001 mg the order is rejected.

test_cases.description: Verify the rejection message displays the formulary maximum daily dose value.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Acetaminophen is 4000 mg.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Order Acetaminophen totalling 6000 mg per day and attempt to sign.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The rejection message states the formulary maximum daily dose of 4000 mg.

requirement.text: The system SHALL lock a user account after 3 consecutive failed login attempts within a 10-minute window and SHALL display a lockout notice naming the account and the lockout duration.

test_cases.description: Verify the account locks after 3 consecutive failed logins within 10 minutes.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t310' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit 3 consecutive failed login attempts for 'user.t310' within 10 minutes.
Step: 2. Attempt a further login using the CORRECT password.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. After the 3th consecutive failure the account is locked.
ExpectedResult: 2. Access is denied despite correct credentials and a lockout notice naming the account and lockout duration is shown.

test_cases.description: Verify a successful login before the threshold resets the counter.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t310' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit 2 failed attempts, then log in with the correct password.
Step: 2. Log out and submit 2 further failed attempts.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. After the correct login the failed-attempt counter resets to 0.
ExpectedResult: 2. The account remains unlocked and no lockout notice appears, because no window contains 3 consecutive failures.

test_cases.description: Verify the 3-attempt / 10-minute boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t310' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit exactly 2 failed attempts within 10 minutes and inspect state.
Step: 2. Submit an 3th failed attempt at minute 9 and inspect state.
Step: 3. For a fresh account submit 2 failures, wait past minute 10, then submit one more.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 2 failures the account remains unlocked.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 3 failures within 10 minutes the account locks and the lockout notice appears.
ExpectedResult: 3. The final failure falls outside the 10-minute window, so the account remains unlocked.

requirement.text: The system SHALL automatically end a clinical session after 5 minutes without user input and SHALL require re-authentication before the chart can be accessed again.

test_cases.description: Verify a session ends after 5 minutes of no input and requires re-authentication.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx5' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 5 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient chart and leave the workstation idle for 5 minutes.
Step: 2. Attempt to scroll the chart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 5 minutes of inactivity the session ends and the chart is hidden.
ExpectedResult: 2. The chart is inaccessible and a re-authentication prompt is displayed; access is restored only after valid credentials.

test_cases.description: Verify input before the timeout keeps the session active.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx5' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 5 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Remain idle for 4 minutes, then click within the chart.
Step: 2. Remain idle for a further 4 minutes, then click within the chart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The session remains active and no prompt appears.
ExpectedResult: 2. The session remains active because each input resets the inactivity timer.

requirement.text: The system SHALL alert the ordering provider when two active medications (Warfarin and Aspirin) have a known major drug-drug interaction, and the alert SHALL name both interacting medications.

test_cases.description: Verify a major drug-drug interaction alert is raised naming both medications.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; interaction database classifies Warfarin + Aspirin as a major interaction.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Confirm Warfarin is active for the test patient.
Step: 2. Order and sign Aspirin for the patient.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Warfarin is shown as active.
ExpectedResult: 2. A major drug-drug interaction alert is presented and the alert text names both Warfarin and Aspirin.

test_cases.description: Verify no alert is raised for a non-interacting pair.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; interaction database classifies Warfarin + Aspirin as a major interaction.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Confirm the patient has an active medication with no known interaction with the ordered drug.
Step: 2. Order and sign a non-interacting medication.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The prior medication is active.
ExpectedResult: 2. The order is signed with no drug-drug interaction alert presented.

test_cases.description: Verify the drug-drug interaction alert text names both interacting medications.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; interaction database classifies Warfarin + Aspirin as a major interaction.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Trigger the Warfarin + Aspirin interaction and inspect the alert text.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The alert text explicitly contains both 'Warfarin' and 'Aspirin' by name.

requirement.text: The system SHALL restrict access to behavioral-health notes to users holding the Behavioral Health role and SHALL deny access to all other roles, recording each denied attempt in the audit log.

test_cases.description: Verify a Behavioral Health role holder can open a behavioral-health notes record.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'auth.t' holds the Behavioral Health role; a behavioral-health notes record exists for the test patient.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Log in as a user holding the Behavioral Health role.
Step: 2. Open the patient's behavioral-health notes.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Behavioral Health role is active.
ExpectedResult: 2. The behavioral-health notes opens and its content is displayed.

test_cases.description: Verify a user without the Behavioral Health role is denied access.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'auth.t' holds the Behavioral Health role; a behavioral-health notes record exists for the test patient.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Log in as a user WITHOUT the Behavioral Health role.
Step: 2. Attempt to open the behavioral-health notes.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Login succeeds without the Behavioral Health role.
ExpectedResult: 2. Access is denied and no behavioral-health notes content is displayed.

test_cases.description: Verify each denied attempt is recorded in the audit log.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'auth.t' holds the Behavioral Health role; a behavioral-health notes record exists for the test patient.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. As a non-Behavioral Health role user attempt to open the behavioral-health notes.
Step: 2. As an auditor query the audit log for denials.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Access is denied.
ExpectedResult: 2. An audit entry recording the denied attempt is present.

requirement.text: The system SHALL calculate a Amoxicillin dose as 10 milligrams per kilogram of the patient's recorded body weight and SHALL round the calculated dose to 1 decimal place(s).

test_cases.description: Verify the Amoxicillin dose is calculated as 10 mg/kg of recorded body weight.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; pediatric patient with a recorded body weight; Amoxicillin dosing is 10 mg/kg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Confirm the recorded body weight is 12.0 kg.
Step: 2. Select weight-based Amoxicillin dosing at 10 mg/kg.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The recorded body weight of 12.0 kg is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The system calculates and displays a dose of 120.0 mg.

test_cases.description: Verify calculation is blocked when no recorded body weight is recorded.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; pediatric patient with a recorded body weight; Amoxicillin dosing is 10 mg/kg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient with NO recorded body weight.
Step: 2. Select weight-based Amoxicillin dosing at 10 mg/kg.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The chart shows no recorded body weight.
ExpectedResult: 2. No dose is calculated; an error states a recorded weight is required and the order cannot be signed.

test_cases.description: Verify the calculated dose is rounded to 1 decimal place(s).
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; pediatric patient with a recorded body weight; Amoxicillin dosing is 10 mg/kg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Set the recorded body weight to 12.345 kg and select 10 mg/kg dosing.
Step: 2. Set the recorded body weight to 12.344 kg and repeat.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The displayed dose is 123.5 mg, rounded to 1 decimal place(s).
ExpectedResult: 2. The displayed dose shows no more than 1 decimal place(s).

requirement.text: The system SHALL require a documented override reason of at least 8 characters when a provider dismisses a high-severity allergy alert, and SHALL store the override reason with the order.

test_cases.description: Verify a high-severity allergy alert can be dismissed with a sufficient override reason.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a high-severity allergy alert.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Trigger the high-severity allergy alert and choose to override.
Step: 2. Enter a override reason of at least 8 characters and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The high-severity allergy alert is presented and a override reason field is shown.
ExpectedResult: 2. The override is accepted and the order is signed.

test_cases.description: Verify the 8-character minimum override reason boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a high-severity allergy alert.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Enter a override reason of 7 characters and confirm.
Step: 2. Enter a override reason of exactly 8 characters and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 7 characters the override is rejected, below the 8-character minimum.
ExpectedResult: 2. At exactly 8 characters the override is accepted.

test_cases.description: Verify the accepted override reason is stored with the order.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a high-severity allergy alert.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Dismiss the high-severity allergy alert with a valid override reason and open the signed order detail.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The stored order detail shows the exact override reason text that was entered.

requirement.text: The system SHALL reject a new patient registration when the supplied medical record number (MRN-A) already exists in the system, and SHALL display the conflicting medical record number in the rejection message.

test_cases.description: Verify a new patient can be registered with a unique medical record number.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; registration clerk logged in.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open Patient Registration -> New Patient.
Step: 2. Enter demographics with a unique medical record number 'MRN-A-0001'.
Step: 3. Click 'Register'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The registration form is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The patient is registered and the chart is created with medical record number 'MRN-A-0001'.

test_cases.description: Verify the rejection message displays the conflicting medical record number.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; registration clerk logged in.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Attempt to register a patient with the duplicate medical record number 'MRN-A-0002'.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The rejection message displays the conflicting medical record number 'MRN-A-0002'.

requirement.text: The system SHALL trigger a sepsis alert when a patient's heart rate exceeds 90 bpm AND the patient's temperature exceeds 38 degrees Celsius within the same 4-hour window.

test_cases.description: Verify a infection warning triggers when both heart rate and temperature exceed thresholds within 4 hours.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record heart rate of 110 bpm at 09:00.
Step: 2. Record temperature of 40 degrees Celsius within the same 4-hour window.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The heart rate is recorded.
ExpectedResult: 2. A infection warning is triggered and displayed for the patient.

test_cases.description: Verify no infection warning triggers when neither value exceeds its threshold.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record heart rate of 85 bpm.
Step: 2. Record temperature of 36 degrees Celsius.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Both values are recorded below threshold.
ExpectedResult: 2. No infection warning is triggered.

test_cases.description: Verify the exact thresholds and the 4-hour window boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record heart rate of exactly 90 bpm and temperature of exactly 38 degrees Celsius.
Step: 2. Record both values above threshold but 4 hours and 1 minute apart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At exactly 90 bpm / 38 degrees Celsius no infection warning triggers (values must strictly exceed).
ExpectedResult: 2. Outside the 4-hour window no infection warning triggers.

test_cases.description: Verify no infection warning triggers when only one factor exceeds its threshold.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record only heart rate above 90 bpm (with temperature normal).
Step: 2. Separately record only temperature above 38 degrees Celsius (with heart rate normal).
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. With only heart rate elevated, no infection warning triggers.
ExpectedResult: 2. With only temperature elevated, no infection warning triggers.

requirement.text: The system SHALL allow a provider to place a laboratory order, SHALL allow selection of a collection priority of STAT or Routine, and SHALL print a specimen label containing the patient's MRN and the laboratory order ID.

test_cases.description: Verify a provider can place a laboratory order with STAT priority.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient chart open.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> laboratory.
Step: 2. Select a test and the collection priority 'STAT'.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The laboratory ordering screen is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The order is created with priority STAT and appears in the patient's active orders.
ExpectedResult: 3. The specimen label wording matches the requirement exactly.

test_cases.description: Verify the order cannot be signed without a collection priority.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient chart open.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> laboratory and select a test.
Step: 2. Leave the collection priority unselected.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. A test is selectable.
ExpectedResult: 2. The order is rejected with a message requiring a priority of STAT or Routine, and no order is created.

requirement.text:
The system SHALL display a 'Isolation Precautions' banner on the patient header when the patient has an active contact-isolation order.

Context: this requirement applies to active contact-isolation orders only; non-active contact-isolation orders are covered elsewhere.

test_cases.description: Verify the 'Isolation Precautions' banner appears for a patient with an active contact-isolation order.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; clinician logged in.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient with an active contact-isolation order.
Step: 2. Inspect the patient header.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The patient chart opens.
ExpectedResult: 2. The 'Isolation Precautions' banner is displayed on the patient header.

requirement.text: The system SHALL require two-factor authentication for any user signing in from an IP address outside the hospital network range, and SHALL grant access only after a valid second factor is supplied.

test_cases.description: Verify two-factor authentication is required and grants access from an external IP.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'dr.ext' enrolled in two-factor authentication; workstation IP outside the hospital network range.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. From an IP outside the hospital network range, enter valid credentials.
Step: 2. Enter a valid second factor code.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The source IP is recognised as outside the hospital network range and a two-factor authentication challenge is presented.
ExpectedResult: 2. The valid second factor is accepted and access is granted.

test_cases.description: Verify the the hospital network range boundary is enforced at the edge of the range.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'dr.ext' enrolled in two-factor authentication; workstation IP outside the hospital network range.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Sign in from the last address inside the hospital network range.
Step: 2. Sign in from the first address outside the hospital network range.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Inside the hospital network range no two-factor authentication is required.
ExpectedResult: 2. Just outside the hospital network range a two-factor authentication challenge is enforced.

requirement.text: The system SHALL archive vital-sign readings older than 30 days to cold storage and SHALL keep archived readings retrievable within 2 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify readings older than 30 days are archived to cold storage and remain retrievable.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Locate a vital-sign reading dated 60 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect its storage tier and open it.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The reading is reported as held in cold storage.
ExpectedResult: 2. Its values are retrieved and displayed within 2 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify readings newer than 30 days are not archived to cold storage.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Locate a vital-sign reading dated 1 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect its storage tier.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The reading is listed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The reading is in active storage and has not been archived to cold storage.

test_cases.description: Verify the 30-day archival boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Inspect a reading dated exactly 30 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect a reading dated exactly 31 days ago.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 30 days the reading is still in active storage.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 31 days the reading has been archived to cold storage.

requirement.text: The system SHALL let a nurse document a medication administration of Ondansetron 4 mg, SHALL capture the administration time, and SHALL block a duplicate medication administration within 15 minutes of the previous one for the same medication.

test_cases.description: Verify a nurse can document a medication administration of Ondansetron 4 mg.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Ondansetron 4 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open the Medication Administration Record.
Step: 2. Select the active Ondansetron 4 mg order and document the administration.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Medication Administration Record is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The medication administration is documented and Ondansetron 4 mg is shown as administered.

test_cases.description: Verify a duplicate medication administration within 15 minutes is blocked.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Ondansetron 4 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Given Ondansetron 4 mg was administered 5 minutes ago, select the same order.
Step: 2. Attempt a second administration and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Ondansetron 4 mg order is selectable.
ExpectedResult: 2. The second administration is blocked citing the duplicate within 15 minutes, and no second record is written.

test_cases.description: Verify the 15-minute duplicate boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Ondansetron 4 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Attempt a second medication administration at exactly 15 minutes after the first.
Step: 2. Attempt a second medication administration at 15 minutes minus 1 second after the first.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At exactly 15 minutes the administration is accepted.
ExpectedResult: 2. Just under 15 minutes the administration is blocked.

test_cases.description: Verify the administration time is captured and persisted.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Ondansetron 4 mg.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Document a medication administration and open the recorded entry.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The recorded entry stores the administration time.

requirement.text: The system SHALL deliver a critical lab value notification for potassium to the ordering provider's secure inbox within 5 minutes of result verification.

test_cases.description: Verify a critical lab value notification for potassium is delivered within 5 minutes of verification.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding potassium order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Verify a critical potassium result and record the verification time.
Step: 2. Open the secure inbox and record the notification arrival time.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The critical potassium result is verified.
ExpectedResult: 2. A critical lab value notification is present in the secure inbox and the interval is at or under 5 minutes.

test_cases.description: Verify duplicate verification events do not create a second notification.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding potassium order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Emit the same verified potassium result twice.
Step: 2. Inspect the secure inbox.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The result is verified twice.
ExpectedResult: 2. Exactly one critical lab value notification is present in the secure inbox; the duplicate is suppressed.

test_cases.description: Verify the 5-minute delivery boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding potassium order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Verify a critical potassium result and measure delivery latency to the secure inbox.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The critical lab value notification is recorded as delivered within 5 minutes of verification.

test_cases.description: Verify the notification routes to the ordering provider specifically.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding potassium order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Verify a critical potassium result ordered by 'dr.t' and inspect the recipient.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The critical lab value notification is routed to the ordering provider's secure inbox, not to any other recipient.

requirement.text: The system SHALL transmit a signed prescription to the selected pharmacy within 30 seconds of signing and SHALL update the order status to 'Sent' upon receiving pharmacy confirmation.

test_cases.description: Verify a signed prescription is transmitted to the selected pharmacy.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Select a medication and destination pharmacy.
Step: 2. Click 'Sign & Send' and observe transmission.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The pharmacy is selected.
ExpectedResult: 2. The signed prescription is transmitted to the selected pharmacy.

test_cases.description: Verify status does not become 'Sent' when the pharmacy is unreachable.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Disable the pharmacy endpoint.
Step: 2. Sign and send a prescription and observe status.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The endpoint is unreachable.
ExpectedResult: 2. Transmission fails, an error is shown, and the status does NOT become 'Sent'.

test_cases.description: Verify transmission occurs within the 30-second limit.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Sign a signed prescription and record the signing time.
Step: 2. Record the arrival time at the pharmacy interface.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The elapsed interval between signing and arrival is at or under 30 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify the order status updates to 'Sent' upon pharmacy confirmation.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Transmit a prescription and have the pharmacy return confirmation.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. On pharmacy confirmation the order status updates to 'Sent'.

requirement.text:
The system SHALL display the mean arterial pressure computed from systolic and diastolic blood pressure on the patient header, rounded to 0 decimal place(s).

Context: handling of missing or invalid systolic and diastolic blood pressure is specified elsewhere.

test_cases.description: Verify mean arterial pressure is computed from systolic and diastolic blood pressure and displayed.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; clinician logged in; test patient has recorded systolic and diastolic blood pressure.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient with recorded systolic and diastolic blood pressure.
Step: 2. Inspect the patient header.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The systolic and diastolic blood pressure are shown.
ExpectedResult: 2. The mean arterial pressure is computed from systolic and diastolic blood pressure and displayed on the patient header.

test_cases.description: Verify the displayed mean arterial pressure is rounded to 0 decimal place(s).
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; clinician logged in; test patient has recorded systolic and diastolic blood pressure.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Set systolic and diastolic blood pressure to values whose mean arterial pressure is non-terminating and inspect the header.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The displayed mean arterial pressure shows no more than 0 decimal place(s).

requirement.text: The system SHALL reject a medication order when the ordered daily dose of Ibuprofen exceeds the formulary maximum daily dose of 3200 mg defined in the formulary, and SHALL display the formulary maximum daily dose in the rejection message.

test_cases.description: Verify a Ibuprofen order within the formulary maximum daily dose is accepted.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Ibuprofen is 3200 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> Medications and select Ibuprofen.
Step: 2. Enter a regimen totalling 1600 mg per day.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The medication ordering screen is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The daily total of 1600 mg is calculated and shown.
ExpectedResult: 3. The order is accepted and saved, within the formulary maximum daily dose of 3200 mg.

test_cases.description: Verify a Ibuprofen order exceeding the formulary maximum daily dose is rejected.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Ibuprofen is 3200 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> Medications and select Ibuprofen.
Step: 2. Enter a regimen totalling 4800 mg per day.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The medication ordering screen is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The daily total of 4800 mg is calculated and shown.
ExpectedResult: 3. The order is rejected and is not saved.

test_cases.description: Verify the formulary maximum daily dose boundary for Ibuprofen.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Ibuprofen is 3200 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Order Ibuprofen totalling exactly 3200 mg per day and sign.
Step: 2. Order Ibuprofen totalling 3201 mg per day and sign.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At exactly 3200 mg the order is accepted, because the dose did not EXCEED the maximum.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 3201 mg the order is rejected.

test_cases.description: Verify the rejection message displays the formulary maximum daily dose value.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Ibuprofen is 3200 mg.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Order Ibuprofen totalling 4800 mg per day and attempt to sign.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The rejection message states the formulary maximum daily dose of 3200 mg.

requirement.text: The system SHALL lock a user account after 3 consecutive failed login attempts within a 15-minute window and SHALL display a lockout notice naming the account and the lockout duration.

test_cases.description: Verify the account locks after 3 consecutive failed logins within 15 minutes.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t315' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit 3 consecutive failed login attempts for 'user.t315' within 15 minutes.
Step: 2. Attempt a further login using the CORRECT password.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. After the 3th consecutive failure the account is locked.
ExpectedResult: 2. Access is denied despite correct credentials and a suspension banner naming the account and lockout duration is shown.

test_cases.description: Verify a successful login before the threshold resets the counter.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t315' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit 2 failed attempts, then log in with the correct password.
Step: 2. Log out and submit 2 further failed attempts.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. After the correct login the failed-attempt counter resets to 0.
ExpectedResult: 2. The account remains unlocked and no suspension banner appears, because no window contains 3 consecutive failures.

test_cases.description: Verify the 3-attempt / 15-minute boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t315' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit exactly 2 failed attempts within 15 minutes and inspect state.
Step: 2. Submit an 3th failed attempt at minute 14 and inspect state.
Step: 3. For a fresh account submit 2 failures, wait past minute 15, then submit one more.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 2 failures the account remains unlocked.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 3 failures within 15 minutes the account locks and the suspension banner appears.
ExpectedResult: 3. The final failure falls outside the 15-minute window, so the account remains unlocked.

requirement.text: The system SHALL automatically end a clinical session after 10 minutes without user input and SHALL require re-authentication before the chart can be accessed again.

test_cases.description: Verify input before the timeout keeps the session active.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx10' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 10 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Remain idle for 9 minutes, then click within the chart.
Step: 2. Remain idle for a further 9 minutes, then click within the chart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The session remains active and no prompt appears.
ExpectedResult: 2. The session remains active because each input resets the inactivity timer.

test_cases.description: Verify the 10-minute inactivity boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx10' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 10 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Remain idle for exactly 10 minutes minus 1 second; inspect state.
Step: 2. Allow inactivity to reach exactly 10 minutes 0 seconds; inspect state.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Just under 10 minutes the session is still active.
ExpectedResult: 2. At exactly 10 minutes the session ends and re-authentication is required.

requirement.text: The system SHALL alert the ordering provider when two active medications (Warfarin and Fluconazole) have a known major drug-drug interaction, and the alert SHALL name both interacting medications.

test_cases.description: Verify a major drug-drug interaction alert is raised naming both medications.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; interaction database classifies Warfarin + Fluconazole as a major interaction.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Confirm Warfarin is active for the test patient.
Step: 2. Order and sign Fluconazole for the patient.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Warfarin is shown as active.
ExpectedResult: 2. A major drug-drug interaction alert is presented and the alert text names both Warfarin and Fluconazole.

test_cases.description: Verify no alert is raised for a non-interacting pair.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; interaction database classifies Warfarin + Fluconazole as a major interaction.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Confirm the patient has an active medication with no known interaction with the ordered drug.
Step: 2. Order and sign a non-interacting medication.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The prior medication is active.
ExpectedResult: 2. The order is signed with no drug-drug interaction alert presented.

test_cases.description: Verify the drug-drug interaction alert text names both interacting medications.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; interaction database classifies Warfarin + Fluconazole as a major interaction.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Trigger the Warfarin + Fluconazole interaction and inspect the alert text.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The alert text explicitly contains both 'Warfarin' and 'Fluconazole' by name.

requirement.text: The system SHALL restrict access to HIV test results to users holding the Infectious Disease role and SHALL deny access to all other roles, recording each denied attempt in the audit log.

test_cases.description: Verify a Infectious Disease role holder can open a HIV test results record.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'auth.t' holds the Infectious Disease role; a HIV test results record exists for the test patient.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Log in as a user holding the Infectious Disease role.
Step: 2. Open the patient's HIV test results.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Infectious Disease role is active.
ExpectedResult: 2. The HIV test results opens and its content is displayed.

test_cases.description: Verify a user without the Infectious Disease role is denied access.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'auth.t' holds the Infectious Disease role; a HIV test results record exists for the test patient.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Log in as a user WITHOUT the Infectious Disease role.
Step: 2. Attempt to open the HIV test results.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Login succeeds without the Infectious Disease role.
ExpectedResult: 2. Access is denied and no HIV test results content is displayed.

test_cases.description: Verify each denied attempt is recorded in the audit log.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'auth.t' holds the Infectious Disease role; a HIV test results record exists for the test patient.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. As a non-Infectious Disease role user attempt to open the HIV test results.
Step: 2. As an auditor query the audit log for denials.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Access is denied.
ExpectedResult: 2. An audit entry recording the denied attempt is present.

requirement.text: The system SHALL calculate a Gentamicin dose as 2 milligrams per kilogram of the patient's recorded body weight and SHALL round the calculated dose to 2 decimal place(s).

test_cases.description: Verify the Gentamicin dose is calculated as 2 mg/kg of recorded body weight.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; pediatric patient with a recorded body weight; Gentamicin dosing is 2 mg/kg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Confirm the recorded body weight is 12.0 kg.
Step: 2. Select weight-based Gentamicin dosing at 2 mg/kg.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The recorded body weight of 12.0 kg is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The system calculates and displays a dose of 24.0 mg.

test_cases.description: Verify calculation is blocked when no recorded body weight is recorded.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; pediatric patient with a recorded body weight; Gentamicin dosing is 2 mg/kg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient with NO recorded body weight.
Step: 2. Select weight-based Gentamicin dosing at 2 mg/kg.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The chart shows no recorded body weight.
ExpectedResult: 2. No dose is calculated; an error states a recorded weight is required and the order cannot be signed.

test_cases.description: Verify the calculated dose is rounded to 2 decimal place(s).
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; pediatric patient with a recorded body weight; Gentamicin dosing is 2 mg/kg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Set the recorded body weight to 12.345 kg and select 2 mg/kg dosing.
Step: 2. Set the recorded body weight to 12.344 kg and repeat.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The displayed dose is 24.69 mg, rounded to 2 decimal place(s).
ExpectedResult: 2. The displayed dose shows no more than 2 decimal place(s).

requirement.text: The system SHALL require a documented override reason of at least 8 characters when a provider dismisses a hard-stop dosing alert, and SHALL store the override reason with the order.

test_cases.description: Verify a hard-stop dosing alert can be dismissed with a sufficient override reason.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a hard-stop dosing alert.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Trigger the hard-stop dosing alert and choose to override.
Step: 2. Enter a override reason of at least 8 characters and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The hard-stop dosing alert is presented and a override reason field is shown.
ExpectedResult: 2. The override is accepted and the order is signed.

test_cases.description: Verify the alert cannot be dismissed with no override reason.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a hard-stop dosing alert.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Trigger the hard-stop dosing alert and choose to override.
Step: 2. Leave the override reason empty and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. A override reason field is shown.
ExpectedResult: 2. The override is rejected, a message requires a override reason, and the order is not signed.

test_cases.description: Verify the 8-character minimum override reason boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a hard-stop dosing alert.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Enter a override reason of 7 characters and confirm.
Step: 2. Enter a override reason of exactly 8 characters and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 7 characters the override is rejected, below the 8-character minimum.
ExpectedResult: 2. At exactly 8 characters the override is accepted.

test_cases.description: Verify the accepted override reason is stored with the order.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a hard-stop dosing alert.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Dismiss the hard-stop dosing alert with a valid override reason and open the signed order detail.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The stored order detail shows the exact override reason text that was entered.

requirement.text: The system SHALL reject a new patient registration when the supplied medical record number (MRN-B) already exists in the system, and SHALL display the conflicting medical record number in the rejection message.

test_cases.description: Verify a new patient can be registered with a unique medical record number.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; registration clerk logged in.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open Patient Registration -> New Patient.
Step: 2. Enter demographics with a unique medical record number 'MRN-B-0001'.
Step: 3. Click 'Register'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The registration form is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The patient is registered and the chart is created with medical record number 'MRN-B-0001'.

test_cases.description: Verify registration is rejected when the medical record number already exists.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; registration clerk logged in.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Seed the system with an existing medical record number 'MRN-B-0002'.
Step: 2. Register a new patient with the same medical record number 'MRN-B-0002'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The existing medical record number is present.
ExpectedResult: 2. The registration is rejected and no new patient record is created.

test_cases.description: Verify the rejection message displays the conflicting medical record number.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; registration clerk logged in.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Attempt to register a patient with the duplicate medical record number 'MRN-B-0002'.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The rejection message displays the conflicting medical record number 'MRN-B-0002'.

requirement.text: The system SHALL trigger a sepsis alert when a patient's respiratory rate exceeds 22 breaths/min AND the patient's temperature exceeds 38 degrees Celsius within the same 6-hour window.

test_cases.description: Verify no sepsis alert triggers when neither value exceeds its threshold.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record respiratory rate of 17 breaths/min.
Step: 2. Record temperature of 36 degrees Celsius.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Both values are recorded below threshold.
ExpectedResult: 2. No sepsis alert is triggered.

test_cases.description: Verify the exact thresholds and the 6-hour window boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record respiratory rate of exactly 22 breaths/min and temperature of exactly 38 degrees Celsius.
Step: 2. Record both values above threshold but 6 hours and 1 minute apart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At exactly 22 breaths/min / 38 degrees Celsius no sepsis alert triggers (values must strictly exceed).
ExpectedResult: 2. Outside the 6-hour window no sepsis alert triggers.

test_cases.description: Verify no sepsis alert triggers when only one factor exceeds its threshold.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record only respiratory rate above 22 breaths/min (with temperature normal).
Step: 2. Separately record only temperature above 38 degrees Celsius (with respiratory rate normal).
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. With only respiratory rate elevated, no sepsis alert triggers.
ExpectedResult: 2. With only temperature elevated, no sepsis alert triggers.

requirement.text: The system SHALL allow a provider to place a radiology order, SHALL allow selection of a collection priority of STAT or Routine, and SHALL print a specimen label containing the patient's MRN and the radiology order ID.

test_cases.description: Verify a provider can place a radiology order with STAT priority.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient chart open.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> radiology.
Step: 2. Select a test and the collection priority 'STAT'.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The radiology ordering screen is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The order is created with priority STAT and appears in the patient's active orders.
ExpectedResult: 3. The specimen label wording matches the requirement exactly.

test_cases.description: Verify the order cannot be signed without a collection priority.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient chart open.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> radiology and select a test.
Step: 2. Leave the collection priority unselected.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. A test is selectable.
ExpectedResult: 2. The order is rejected with a message requiring a priority of STAT or Routine, and no order is created.

requirement.text:
The system SHALL display a 'Fall Risk' banner on the patient header when the patient has an active fall-risk order.

Context: this requirement applies to active fall-risk orders only; non-active fall-risk orders are covered elsewhere.

test_cases.description: Verify the 'Fall Risk' banner appears for a patient with an active fall-risk order.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; clinician logged in.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient with an active fall-risk order.
Step: 2. Inspect the patient header.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The patient chart opens.
ExpectedResult: 2. The 'Fall Risk' banner is displayed on the patient header.

test_cases.description: Verify the 'Fall Risk' banner is absent when no active fall-risk order exists.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; clinician logged in.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient with no active fall-risk order.
Step: 2. Inspect the patient header.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The patient chart opens.
ExpectedResult: 2. The 'Fall Risk' banner is not displayed.

requirement.text: The system SHALL require two-factor authentication for any user signing in from an IP address outside the campus 10.0.0.0/8 range, and SHALL grant access only after a valid second factor is supplied.

test_cases.description: Verify two-factor authentication is required and grants access from an external IP.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'dr.ext' enrolled in two-factor authentication; workstation IP outside the campus 10.0.0.0/8 range.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. From an IP outside the campus 10.0.0.0/8 range, enter valid credentials.
Step: 2. Enter a valid second factor code.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The source IP is recognised as outside the campus 10.0.0.0/8 range and a two-factor authentication challenge is presented.
ExpectedResult: 2. The valid second factor is accepted and access is granted.

test_cases.description: Verify an invalid second factor denies access.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'dr.ext' enrolled in two-factor authentication; workstation IP outside the campus 10.0.0.0/8 range.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. From an IP outside the campus 10.0.0.0/8 range, enter valid credentials.
Step: 2. Enter an INVALID second factor code.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. A two-factor authentication challenge is presented.
ExpectedResult: 2. The invalid second factor is rejected and access is denied.

test_cases.description: Verify the the campus 10.0.0.0/8 range boundary is enforced at the edge of the range.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'dr.ext' enrolled in two-factor authentication; workstation IP outside the campus 10.0.0.0/8 range.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Sign in from the last address inside the campus 10.0.0.0/8 range.
Step: 2. Sign in from the first address outside the campus 10.0.0.0/8 range.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Inside the campus 10.0.0.0/8 range no two-factor authentication is required.
ExpectedResult: 2. Just outside the campus 10.0.0.0/8 range a two-factor authentication challenge is enforced.

requirement.text: The system SHALL archive vital-sign readings older than 30 days to cold storage and SHALL keep archived readings retrievable within 5 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify readings older than 30 days are archived to cold storage and remain retrievable.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Locate a vital-sign reading dated 60 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect its storage tier and open it.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The reading is reported as held in cold storage.
ExpectedResult: 2. Its values are retrieved and displayed within 5 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify readings newer than 30 days are not archived to cold storage.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Locate a vital-sign reading dated 1 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect its storage tier.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The reading is listed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The reading is in active storage and has not been archived to cold storage.

requirement.text: The system SHALL let a nurse document a medication administration of Morphine 2 mg, SHALL capture the administration time, and SHALL block a duplicate medication administration within 15 minutes of the previous one for the same medication.

test_cases.description: Verify a nurse can document a medication handoff of Morphine 2 mg.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Morphine 2 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open the Medication Administration Record.
Step: 2. Select the active Morphine 2 mg order and document the administration.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Medication Administration Record is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The medication handoff is documented and Morphine 2 mg is shown as administered.

test_cases.description: Verify a duplicate medication handoff within 15 minutes is blocked.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Morphine 2 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Given Morphine 2 mg was administered 5 minutes ago, select the same order.
Step: 2. Attempt a second administration and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Morphine 2 mg order is selectable.
ExpectedResult: 2. The second administration is blocked citing the duplicate within 15 minutes, and no second record is written.

test_cases.description: Verify the 15-minute duplicate boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Morphine 2 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Attempt a second medication handoff at exactly 15 minutes after the first.
Step: 2. Attempt a second medication handoff at 15 minutes minus 1 second after the first.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At exactly 15 minutes the administration is accepted.
ExpectedResult: 2. Just under 15 minutes the administration is blocked.

test_cases.description: Verify the administration time is captured and persisted.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Morphine 2 mg.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Document a medication handoff and open the recorded entry.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The recorded entry stores the administration time.

requirement.text: The system SHALL deliver a critical lab value notification for troponin to the ordering provider's secure inbox within 5 minutes of result verification.

test_cases.description: Verify a critical lab value notification for troponin is delivered within 5 minutes of verification.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding troponin order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Verify a critical troponin result and record the verification time.
Step: 2. Open the secure inbox and record the notification arrival time.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The critical troponin result is verified.
ExpectedResult: 2. A critical lab value notification is present in the secure inbox and the interval is at or under 5 minutes.

test_cases.description: Verify duplicate verification events do not create a second notification.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding troponin order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Emit the same verified troponin result twice.
Step: 2. Inspect the secure inbox.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The result is verified twice.
ExpectedResult: 2. Exactly one critical lab value notification is present in the secure inbox; the duplicate is suppressed.

test_cases.description: Verify the notification routes to the ordering provider specifically.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding troponin order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Verify a critical troponin result ordered by 'dr.t' and inspect the recipient.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The critical lab value notification is routed to the ordering provider's secure inbox, not to any other recipient.

requirement.text: The system SHALL transmit a signed prescription to the selected pharmacy within 45 seconds of signing and SHALL update the order status to 'Sent' upon receiving pharmacy confirmation.

test_cases.description: Verify a signed prescription is transmitted to the selected pharmacy.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Select a medication and destination pharmacy.
Step: 2. Click 'Sign & Send' and observe transmission.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The pharmacy is selected.
ExpectedResult: 2. The signed prescription is transmitted to the selected pharmacy.

test_cases.description: Verify status does not become 'Sent' when the pharmacy is unreachable.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Disable the pharmacy endpoint.
Step: 2. Sign and send a prescription and observe status.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The endpoint is unreachable.
ExpectedResult: 2. Transmission fails, an error is shown, and the status does NOT become 'Sent'.

test_cases.description: Verify transmission occurs within the 45-second limit.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Sign a signed prescription and record the signing time.
Step: 2. Record the arrival time at the pharmacy interface.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The elapsed interval between signing and arrival is at or under 45 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify the order status updates to 'Sent' upon pharmacy confirmation.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Transmit a prescription and have the pharmacy return confirmation.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. On pharmacy confirmation the order status updates to 'Sent'.

requirement.text:
The system SHALL display the body mass index computed from height and weight on the patient header, rounded to 1 decimal place(s).

Context: handling of missing or invalid height and weight is specified elsewhere.

test_cases.description: Verify body mass index is computed from height and weight and displayed.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; clinician logged in; test patient has recorded height and weight.

ExpectedResult: 1. The height and weight are shown.

test_cases.description: Verify the displayed body mass index is rounded to 1 decimal place(s).
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; clinician logged in; test patient has recorded height and weight.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Set height and weight to values whose body mass index is non-terminating and inspect the header.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The displayed body mass index shows no more than 1 decimal place(s).

requirement.text: The system SHALL reject a medication order when the ordered daily dose of Metformin exceeds the formulary maximum daily dose of 2550 mg defined in the formulary, and SHALL display the formulary maximum daily dose in the rejection message.

test_cases.description: Verify a Metformin order within the formulary maximum daily dose is accepted.

test_cases.description: Verify a Metformin order exceeding the formulary maximum daily dose is rejected.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Metformin is 2550 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> Medications and select Metformin.
Step: 2. Enter a regimen totalling 3825 mg per day.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The medication ordering screen is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The daily total of 3825 mg is calculated and shown.
ExpectedResult: 3. The order is rejected and is not saved.

test_cases.description: Verify the rejection message displays the formulary maximum daily dose value.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Metformin is 2550 mg.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Order Metformin totalling 3825 mg per day and attempt to sign.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The rejection message states the formulary maximum daily dose of 2550 mg.

requirement.text: The system SHALL lock a user account after 3 consecutive failed login attempts within a 20-minute window and SHALL display a lockout notice naming the account and the lockout duration.

test_cases.description: Verify the account locks after 3 consecutive failed logins within 20 minutes.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t320' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit 3 consecutive failed login attempts for 'user.t320' within 20 minutes.
Step: 2. Attempt a further login using the CORRECT password.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. After the 3th consecutive failure the account is locked.
ExpectedResult: 2. Access is denied despite correct credentials and a lockout notice naming the account and lockout duration is shown.

test_cases.description: Verify a successful login before the threshold resets the counter.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t320' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit 2 failed attempts, then log in with the correct password.
Step: 2. Log out and submit 2 further failed attempts.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. After the correct login the failed-attempt counter resets to 0.
ExpectedResult: 2. The account remains unlocked and no lockout notice appears, because no window contains 3 consecutive failures.

test_cases.description: Verify the 3-attempt / 20-minute boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t320' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit exactly 2 failed attempts within 20 minutes and inspect state.
Step: 2. Submit an 3th failed attempt at minute 19 and inspect state.
Step: 3. For a fresh account submit 2 failures, wait past minute 20, then submit one more.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 2 failures the account remains unlocked.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 3 failures within 20 minutes the account locks and the lockout notice appears.
ExpectedResult: 3. The final failure falls outside the 20-minute window, so the account remains unlocked.

requirement.text: The system SHALL automatically end a clinical session after 15 minutes without user input and SHALL require re-authentication before the chart can be accessed again.

test_cases.description: Verify a session ends after 15 minutes of no input and requires re-authentication.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx15' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 15 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient chart and leave the workstation idle for 15 minutes.
Step: 2. Attempt to scroll the chart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 15 minutes of inactivity the session ends and the chart is hidden.
ExpectedResult: 2. The chart is inaccessible and a re-authentication prompt is displayed; access is restored only after valid credentials.

test_cases.description: Verify input before the timeout keeps the session active.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx15' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 15 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Remain idle for 14 minutes, then click within the chart.
Step: 2. Remain idle for a further 14 minutes, then click within the chart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The session remains active and no prompt appears.
ExpectedResult: 2. The session remains active because each input resets the inactivity timer.

test_cases.description: Verify the 15-minute inactivity boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx15' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 15 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Remain idle for exactly 15 minutes minus 1 second; inspect state.
Step: 2. Allow inactivity to reach exactly 15 minutes 0 seconds; inspect state.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Just under 15 minutes the session is still active.
ExpectedResult: 2. At exactly 15 minutes the session ends and re-authentication is required.

requirement.text: The system SHALL alert the ordering provider when two active medications (Clopidogrel and Omeprazole) have a known major drug-drug interaction, and the alert SHALL name both interacting medications.

test_cases.description: Verify a major drug-drug interaction alert is raised naming both medications.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; interaction database classifies Clopidogrel + Omeprazole as a major interaction.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Confirm Clopidogrel is active for the test patient.
Step: 2. Order and sign Omeprazole for the patient.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Clopidogrel is shown as active.
ExpectedResult: 2. A major drug-drug interaction alert is presented and the alert text names both Clopidogrel and Omeprazole.

test_cases.description: Verify no alert is raised for a non-interacting pair.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; interaction database classifies Clopidogrel + Omeprazole as a major interaction.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Confirm the patient has an active medication with no known interaction with the ordered drug.
Step: 2. Order and sign a non-interacting medication.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The prior medication is active.
ExpectedResult: 2. The order is signed with no drug-drug interaction alert presented.

requirement.text: The system SHALL restrict access to genetic test results to users holding the Genetic Counseling role and SHALL deny access to all other roles, recording each denied attempt in the audit log.

test_cases.description: Verify a Genetic Counseling role holder can open a genetic test results record.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'auth.t' holds the Genetic Counseling role; a genetic test results record exists for the test patient.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Log in as a user holding the Genetic Counseling role.
Step: 2. Open the patient's genetic test results.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Genetic Counseling role is active.
ExpectedResult: 2. The genetic test results opens and its content is displayed.

test_cases.description: Verify a user without the Genetic Counseling role is denied access.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'auth.t' holds the Genetic Counseling role; a genetic test results record exists for the test patient.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Log in as a user WITHOUT the Genetic Counseling role.
Step: 2. Attempt to open the genetic test results.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Login succeeds without the Genetic Counseling role.
ExpectedResult: 2. Access is denied and no genetic test results content is displayed.

requirement.text: The system SHALL calculate a Vancomycin dose as 15 milligrams per kilogram of the patient's recorded body weight and SHALL round the calculated dose to 1 decimal place(s).

test_cases.description: Verify the Vancomycin dose is calculated as 15 mg/kg of recorded body weight.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; pediatric patient with a recorded body weight; Vancomycin dosing is 15 mg/kg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Confirm the recorded body weight is 12.0 kg.
Step: 2. Select weight-based Vancomycin dosing at 15 mg/kg.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The recorded body weight of 12.0 kg is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The system calculates and displays a dose of 180.0 mg.

test_cases.description: Verify calculation is blocked when no recorded body weight is recorded.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; pediatric patient with a recorded body weight; Vancomycin dosing is 15 mg/kg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient with NO recorded body weight.
Step: 2. Select weight-based Vancomycin dosing at 15 mg/kg.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The chart shows no recorded body weight.
ExpectedResult: 2. No dose is calculated; an error states a recorded weight is required and the order cannot be signed.

test_cases.description: Verify the calculated dose is rounded to 1 decimal place(s).
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; pediatric patient with a recorded body weight; Vancomycin dosing is 15 mg/kg.
test_cases.steps:

Step: 2. Set the recorded body weight to 12.344 kg and repeat.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The displayed dose is 185.2 mg, rounded to 1 decimal place(s).
ExpectedResult: 2. The displayed dose shows no more than 1 decimal place(s).

requirement.text: The system SHALL require a documented override reason of at least 8 characters when a provider dismisses a critical drug-interaction alert, and SHALL store the override reason with the order.

test_cases.description: Verify a critical drug-interaction alert can be dismissed with a sufficient override reason.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a critical drug-interaction alert.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Trigger the critical drug-interaction alert and choose to override.
Step: 2. Enter a override reason of at least 8 characters and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The critical drug-interaction alert is presented and a override reason field is shown.
ExpectedResult: 2. The override is accepted and the order is signed.

test_cases.description: Verify the alert cannot be dismissed with no override reason.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a critical drug-interaction alert.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Trigger the critical drug-interaction alert and choose to override.
Step: 2. Leave the override reason empty and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. A override reason field is shown.
ExpectedResult: 2. The override is rejected, a message requires a override reason, and the order is not signed.

test_cases.description: Verify the 8-character minimum override reason boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a critical drug-interaction alert.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Enter a override reason of 7 characters and confirm.
Step: 2. Enter a override reason of exactly 8 characters and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 7 characters the override is rejected, below the 8-character minimum.

test_cases.description: Verify the accepted override reason is stored with the order.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a critical drug-interaction alert.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Dismiss the critical drug-interaction alert with a valid override reason and open the signed order detail.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The stored order detail shows the exact override reason text that was entered.

requirement.text: The system SHALL reject a new patient registration when the supplied medical record number (MRN-C) already exists in the system, and SHALL display the conflicting medical record number in the rejection message.

requirement.text: The system SHALL trigger a sepsis alert when a patient's systolic blood pressure exceeds 180 mmHg AND the patient's heart rate exceeds 110 bpm within the same 2-hour window.

test_cases.description: Verify a sepsis alert triggers when both systolic blood pressure and heart rate exceed thresholds within 2 hours.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record systolic blood pressure of 218 mmHg at 09:00.
Step: 2. Record heart rate of 112 bpm within the same 2-hour window.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The systolic blood pressure is recorded.
ExpectedResult: 2. A sepsis alert is triggered and displayed for the patient.

test_cases.description: Verify no sepsis alert triggers when neither value exceeds its threshold.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record systolic blood pressure of 175 mmHg.
Step: 2. Record heart rate of 108 bpm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Both values are recorded below threshold.
ExpectedResult: 2. No sepsis alert is triggered.

test_cases.description: Verify the exact thresholds and the 2-hour window boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record systolic blood pressure of exactly 180 mmHg and heart rate of exactly 110 bpm.
Step: 2. Record both values above threshold but 2 hours and 1 minute apart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At exactly 180 mmHg / 110 bpm no sepsis alert triggers (values must strictly exceed).
ExpectedResult: 2. Outside the 2-hour window no sepsis alert triggers.

test_cases.description: Verify no sepsis alert triggers when only one factor exceeds its threshold.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record only systolic blood pressure above 180 mmHg (with heart rate normal).
Step: 2. Separately record only heart rate above 110 bpm (with systolic blood pressure normal).
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. With only systolic blood pressure elevated, no sepsis alert triggers.
ExpectedResult: 2. With only heart rate elevated, no sepsis alert triggers.

requirement.text: The system SHALL allow a provider to place a microbiology order, SHALL allow selection of a collection priority of STAT or Routine, and SHALL print a specimen label containing the patient's MRN and the microbiology order ID.

test_cases.description: Verify a provider can place a microbiology order with STAT priority.

test_cases.description: Verify the order cannot be signed without a collection priority.

Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> microbiology and select a test.

test_cases.expectedResults:

ExpectedResult: 2. The order is rejected with a message requiring a priority of STAT or Routine, and no order is created.

requirement.text:
The system SHALL display a 'DNR' banner on the patient header when the patient has an active do-not-resuscitate order.
