requirement.text: The system SHALL require two-factor authentication for any user signing in from an IP address outside the internal enterprise range, and SHALL grant access only after a valid second factor is supplied.

test_cases.description: Verify an invalid second factor denies access.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'dr.ext' enrolled in two-factor authentication; workstation IP outside the internal enterprise range.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. From an IP outside the internal enterprise range, enter valid credentials.
Step: 2. Enter an INVALID second factor code.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. A two-factor authentication challenge is presented.
ExpectedResult: 2. The invalid second factor is rejected and access is denied.

test_cases.description: Verify the the internal enterprise range boundary is enforced at the edge of the range.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'dr.ext' enrolled in two-factor authentication; workstation IP outside the internal enterprise range.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Sign in from the last address inside the internal enterprise range.
Step: 2. Sign in from the first address outside the internal enterprise range.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Inside the internal enterprise range no two-factor authentication is required.
ExpectedResult: 2. Just outside the internal enterprise range a two-factor authentication challenge is enforced.

requirement.text: The system SHALL archive vital-sign readings older than 60 days to cold storage and SHALL keep archived readings retrievable within 2 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify readings older than 60 days are archived to cold storage and remain retrievable.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Locate a vital-sign reading dated 90 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect its storage tier and open it.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The reading is reported as held in cold storage.
ExpectedResult: 2. Its values are retrieved and displayed within 2 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify readings newer than 60 days are not archived to cold storage.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Locate a vital-sign reading dated 1 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect its storage tier.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The reading is listed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The reading is in active storage and has not been archived to cold storage.

test_cases.description: Verify the 60-day archival boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Inspect a reading dated exactly 60 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect a reading dated exactly 61 days ago.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 60 days the reading is still in active storage.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 61 days the reading has been archived to cold storage.

requirement.text: The system SHALL let a nurse document a medication administration of Ondansetron 4 mg, SHALL capture the administration time, and SHALL block a duplicate medication administration within 30 minutes of the previous one for the same medication.

test_cases.description: Verify a nurse can document a medication handoff of Ondansetron 4 mg.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Ondansetron 4 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open the Medication Administration Record.
Step: 2. Select the active Ondansetron 4 mg order and document the administration.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Medication Administration Record is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The medication handoff is documented and Ondansetron 4 mg is shown as administered.

test_cases.description: Verify a duplicate medication handoff within 30 minutes is blocked.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Ondansetron 4 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Given Ondansetron 4 mg was administered 5 minutes ago, select the same order.
Step: 2. Attempt a second administration and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Ondansetron 4 mg order is selectable.
ExpectedResult: 2. The second administration is blocked citing the duplicate within 30 minutes, and no second record is written.

test_cases.description: Verify the 30-minute duplicate boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Ondansetron 4 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Attempt a second medication handoff at exactly 30 minutes after the first.
Step: 2. Attempt a second medication handoff at 30 minutes minus 1 second after the first.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At exactly 30 minutes the administration is accepted.
ExpectedResult: 2. Just under 30 minutes the administration is blocked.

test_cases.description: Verify the administration time is captured and persisted.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Ondansetron 4 mg.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Document a medication handoff and open the recorded entry.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The recorded entry stores the administration time.

requirement.text: The system SHALL deliver a critical lab value notification for sodium to the ordering provider's secure inbox within 5 minutes of result verification.

test_cases.description: Verify a critical lab value notification for sodium is delivered within 5 minutes of verification.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding sodium order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Verify a critical sodium result and record the verification time.
Step: 2. Open the secure inbox and record the notification arrival time.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The critical sodium result is verified.
ExpectedResult: 2. A critical lab value notification is present in the secure inbox and the interval is at or under 5 minutes.

test_cases.description: Verify duplicate verification events do not create a second notification.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding sodium order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Emit the same verified sodium result twice.
Step: 2. Inspect the secure inbox.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The result is verified twice.
ExpectedResult: 2. Exactly one critical lab value notification is present in the secure inbox; the duplicate is suppressed.

test_cases.description: Verify the 5-minute delivery boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding sodium order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Verify a critical sodium result and measure delivery latency to the secure inbox.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The critical lab value notification is recorded as delivered within 5 minutes of verification.

test_cases.description: Verify the notification routes to the ordering provider specifically.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding sodium order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Verify a critical sodium result ordered by 'dr.t' and inspect the recipient.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The critical lab value notification is routed to the ordering provider's secure inbox, not to any other recipient.

requirement.text: The system SHALL transmit a signed prescription to the selected pharmacy within 20 seconds of signing and SHALL update the order status to 'Sent' upon receiving pharmacy confirmation.

test_cases.description: Verify a signed prescription is transmitted to the selected pharmacy.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Select a medication and destination pharmacy.
Step: 2. Click 'Sign & Send' and observe transmission.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The pharmacy is selected.
ExpectedResult: 2. The signed prescription is transmitted to the selected pharmacy.

test_cases.description: Verify status does not become 'Sent' when the pharmacy is unreachable.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Disable the pharmacy endpoint.
Step: 2. Sign and send a prescription and observe status.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The endpoint is unreachable.
ExpectedResult: 2. Transmission fails, an error is shown, and the status does NOT become 'Sent'.

test_cases.description: Verify transmission occurs within the 20-second limit.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Sign a signed prescription and record the signing time.
Step: 2. Record the arrival time at the pharmacy interface.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The elapsed interval between signing and arrival is at or under 20 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify the order status updates to 'Sent' upon pharmacy confirmation.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Transmit a prescription and have the pharmacy return confirmation.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. On pharmacy confirmation the order status updates to 'Sent'.

requirement.text:
The system SHALL display the anion gap computed from sodium, chloride and bicarbonate on the patient header, rounded to 0 decimal place(s).

Context: handling of missing or invalid sodium, chloride and bicarbonate is specified elsewhere.

test_cases.description: Verify the displayed anion gap is rounded to 0 decimal place(s).
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; clinician logged in; test patient has recorded sodium, chloride and bicarbonate.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Set sodium, chloride and bicarbonate to values whose anion gap is non-terminating and inspect the header.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The displayed anion gap shows no more than 0 decimal place(s).

requirement.text: The system SHALL reject a medication order when the ordered daily dose of Furosemide exceeds the formulary maximum daily dose of 600 mg defined in the formulary, and SHALL display the formulary maximum daily dose in the rejection message.

test_cases.description: Verify a Furosemide order within the formulary maximum daily dose is accepted.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Furosemide is 600 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> Medications and select Furosemide.
Step: 2. Enter a regimen totalling 300 mg per day.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The medication ordering screen is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The daily total of 300 mg is calculated and shown.
ExpectedResult: 3. The order is accepted and saved, within the formulary maximum daily dose of 600 mg.

test_cases.description: Verify a Furosemide order exceeding the formulary maximum daily dose is rejected.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Furosemide is 600 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> Medications and select Furosemide.
Step: 2. Enter a regimen totalling 900 mg per day.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The medication ordering screen is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The daily total of 900 mg is calculated and shown.
ExpectedResult: 3. The order is rejected and is not saved.

test_cases.description: Verify the formulary maximum daily dose boundary for Furosemide.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Furosemide is 600 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Order Furosemide totalling exactly 600 mg per day and sign.
Step: 2. Order Furosemide totalling 601 mg per day and sign.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At exactly 600 mg the order is accepted, because the dose did not EXCEED the maximum.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 601 mg the order is rejected.

test_cases.description: Verify the rejection message displays the formulary maximum daily dose value.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Furosemide is 600 mg.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Order Furosemide totalling 900 mg per day and attempt to sign.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The rejection message states the formulary maximum daily dose of 600 mg.

requirement.text: The system SHALL lock a user account after 4 consecutive failed login attempts within a 30-minute window and SHALL display a lockout notice naming the account and the lockout duration.

test_cases.description: Verify the account locks after 4 consecutive failed logins within 30 minutes.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t430' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit 4 consecutive failed login attempts for 'user.t430' within 30 minutes.
Step: 2. Attempt a further login using the CORRECT password.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. After the 4th consecutive failure the account is locked.
ExpectedResult: 2. Access is denied despite correct credentials and a lockout notice naming the account and lockout duration is shown.

test_cases.description: Verify the 4-attempt / 30-minute boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t430' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit exactly 3 failed attempts within 30 minutes and inspect state.
Step: 2. Submit an 4th failed attempt at minute 29 and inspect state.
Step: 3. For a fresh account submit 3 failures, wait past minute 30, then submit one more.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 3 failures the account remains unlocked.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 4 failures within 30 minutes the account locks and the lockout notice appears.
ExpectedResult: 3. The final failure falls outside the 30-minute window, so the account remains unlocked.

requirement.text: The system SHALL automatically end a clinical session after 60 minutes without user input and SHALL require re-authentication before the chart can be accessed again.

test_cases.description: Verify a session ends after 60 minutes of no input and requires re-authentication.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx60' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 60 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient chart and leave the workstation idle for 60 minutes.
Step: 2. Attempt to scroll the chart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 60 minutes of inactivity the session ends and the chart is hidden.
ExpectedResult: 2. The chart is inaccessible and a re-authentication prompt is displayed; access is restored only after valid credentials.

test_cases.description: Verify input before the timeout keeps the session active.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx60' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 60 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Remain idle for 59 minutes, then click within the chart.
Step: 2. Remain idle for a further 59 minutes, then click within the chart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The session remains active and no prompt appears.
ExpectedResult: 2. The session remains active because each input resets the inactivity timer.

test_cases.description: Verify the 60-minute inactivity boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx60' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 60 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Remain idle for exactly 60 minutes minus 1 second; inspect state.
Step: 2. Allow inactivity to reach exactly 60 minutes 0 seconds; inspect state.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Just under 60 minutes the session is still active.
ExpectedResult: 2. At exactly 60 minutes the session ends and re-authentication is required.

requirement.text: The system SHALL alert the ordering provider when two active medications (Sildenafil and Nitroglycerin) have a known major drug-drug interaction, and the alert SHALL name both interacting medications.

test_cases.description: Verify a major drug-drug interaction alert is raised naming both medications.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; interaction database classifies Sildenafil + Nitroglycerin as a major interaction.

Step: 2. Order and sign Nitroglycerin for the patient.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Sildenafil is shown as active.
ExpectedResult: 2. A major drug-drug interaction alert is presented and the alert text names both Sildenafil and Nitroglycerin.

test_cases.description: Verify no alert is raised for a non-interacting pair.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; interaction database classifies Sildenafil + Nitroglycerin as a major interaction.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Confirm the patient has an active medication with no known interaction with the ordered drug.
Step: 2. Order and sign a non-interacting medication.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The prior medication is active.
ExpectedResult: 2. The order is signed with no drug-drug interaction alert presented.

requirement.text: The system SHALL restrict access to employee-patient charts to users holding the Occupational Health role and SHALL deny access to all other roles, recording each denied attempt in the audit log.

test_cases.description: Verify a Occupational Health role holder can open a employee-patient charts record.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'auth.t' holds the Occupational Health role; a employee-patient charts record exists for the test patient.
test_cases.steps:

Step: 2. Open the patient's employee-patient charts.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Occupational Health role is active.
ExpectedResult: 2. The employee-patient charts opens and its content is displayed.

test_cases.description: Verify a user without the Occupational Health role is denied access.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'auth.t' holds the Occupational Health role; a employee-patient charts record exists for the test patient.
test_cases.steps:

Step: 2. Attempt to open the employee-patient charts.
test_cases.expectedResults:

requirement.text: The system SHALL calculate a Furosemide dose as 1 milligrams per kilogram of the patient's recorded body weight and SHALL round the calculated dose to 1 decimal place(s).

test_cases.description: Verify the Furosemide dose is calculated as 1 mg/kg of recorded body weight.

test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The recorded body weight of 12.0 kg is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The system calculates and displays a dose of 12.0 mg.

test_cases.description: Verify calculation is blocked when no recorded body weight is recorded.

Step: 1. Open a patient with NO recorded body weight.
Step: 2. Select weight-based Furosemide dosing at 1 mg/kg.
test_cases.expectedResults:

test_cases.description: Verify the alert cannot be dismissed with no override reason.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a duplicate-therapy alert.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Trigger the duplicate-therapy alert and choose to override.
Step: 2. Leave the override reason empty and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. A override reason field is shown.
ExpectedResult: 2. The override is rejected, a message requires a override reason, and the order is not signed.

test_cases.description: Verify the 10-character minimum override reason boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a duplicate-therapy alert.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Enter a override reason of 9 characters and confirm.
Step: 2. Enter a override reason of exactly 10 characters and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 9 characters the override is rejected, below the 10-character minimum.
ExpectedResult: 2. At exactly 10 characters the override is accepted.

test_cases.description: Verify the accepted override reason is stored with the order.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a duplicate-therapy alert.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Dismiss the duplicate-therapy alert with a valid override reason and open the signed order detail.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The stored order detail shows the exact override reason text that was entered.

requirement.text: The system SHALL reject a new patient registration when the supplied medical record number (MRN-H) already exists in the system, and SHALL display the conflicting medical record number in the rejection message.

test_cases.description: Verify a new patient can be registered with a unique medical record number.

test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The registration form is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The patient is registered and the chart is created with medical record number 'MRN-H-0001'.

test_cases.description: Verify registration is rejected when the medical record number already exists.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; registration clerk logged in.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Seed the system with an existing medical record number 'MRN-H-0002'.
Step: 2. Register a new patient with the same medical record number 'MRN-H-0002'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The existing medical record number is present.
ExpectedResult: 2. The registration is rejected and no new patient record is created.

test_cases.description: Verify the rejection message displays the conflicting medical record number.

test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Attempt to register a patient with the duplicate medical record number 'MRN-H-0002'.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The rejection message displays the conflicting medical record number 'MRN-H-0002'.

requirement.text: The system SHALL trigger a sepsis alert when a patient's systolic blood pressure exceeds 90 mmHg AND the patient's respiratory rate exceeds 24 breaths/min within the same 4-hour window.

test_cases.description: Verify a sepsis alert triggers when both systolic blood pressure and respiratory rate exceed thresholds within 4 hours.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record systolic blood pressure of 110 mmHg at 09:00.
Step: 2. Record respiratory rate of 26 breaths/min within the same 4-hour window.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The systolic blood pressure is recorded.
ExpectedResult: 2. A sepsis alert is triggered and displayed for the patient.

test_cases.description: Verify no sepsis alert triggers when neither value exceeds its threshold.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record systolic blood pressure of 85 mmHg.
Step: 2. Record respiratory rate of 22 breaths/min.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Both values are recorded below threshold.
ExpectedResult: 2. No sepsis alert is triggered.

test_cases.description: Verify the exact thresholds and the 4-hour window boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record systolic blood pressure of exactly 90 mmHg and respiratory rate of exactly 24 breaths/min.
Step: 2. Record both values above threshold but 4 hours and 1 minute apart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At exactly 90 mmHg / 24 breaths/min no sepsis alert triggers (values must strictly exceed).
ExpectedResult: 2. Outside the 4-hour window no sepsis alert triggers.

requirement.text: The system SHALL allow a provider to place a pulmonary-function order, SHALL allow selection of a collection priority of STAT or Routine, and SHALL print a specimen label containing the patient's MRN and the pulmonary-function order ID.

test_cases.description: Verify a provider can place a pulmonary-function order with STAT priority.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient chart open.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> pulmonary-function.
Step: 2. Select a test and the collection priority 'STAT'.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The pulmonary-function ordering screen is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The order is created with priority STAT and appears in the patient's active orders.
ExpectedResult: 3. The specimen label wording matches the requirement exactly.

test_cases.description: Verify the order cannot be signed without a collection priority.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient chart open.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> pulmonary-function and select a test.
Step: 2. Leave the collection priority unselected.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. A test is selectable.
ExpectedResult: 2. The order is rejected with a message requiring a priority of STAT or Routine, and no order is created.

test_cases.description: Verify Routine priority and the specimen label content.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient chart open.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Place the order with the collection priority 'Routine' and sign.
Step: 2. Inspect the printed specimen label.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The order is created with priority Routine.
ExpectedResult: 2. The specimen label contains the patient's MRN and the pulmonary-function order ID.

requirement.text:
The system SHALL display a 'Safety Watch' banner on the patient header when the patient has an active suicide-watch order.

Context: this requirement applies to active suicide-watch orders only; non-active suicide-watch orders are covered elsewhere.

test_cases.description: Verify the 'Safety Watch' banner appears for a patient with an active suicide-watch order.

test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient with an active suicide-watch order.
Step: 2. Inspect the patient header.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The patient chart opens.
ExpectedResult: 2. The 'Safety Watch' banner is displayed on the patient header.

test_cases.description: Verify the 'Safety Watch' banner is absent when no active suicide-watch order exists.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; clinician logged in.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient with no active suicide-watch order.

test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The patient chart opens.
ExpectedResult: 2. The 'Safety Watch' banner is not displayed.

requirement.text: The system SHALL require two-factor authentication for any user signing in from an IP address outside the primary data-center range, and SHALL grant access only after a valid second factor is supplied.

test_cases.description: Verify two-factor authentication is required and grants access from an external IP.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'dr.ext' enrolled in two-factor authentication; workstation IP outside the primary data-center range.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. From an IP outside the primary data-center range, enter valid credentials.
Step: 2. Enter a valid second factor code.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The source IP is recognised as outside the primary data-center range and a two-factor authentication challenge is presented.
ExpectedResult: 2. The valid second factor is accepted and access is granted.

test_cases.description: Verify the the primary data-center range boundary is enforced at the edge of the range.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'dr.ext' enrolled in two-factor authentication; workstation IP outside the primary data-center range.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Sign in from the last address inside the primary data-center range.
Step: 2. Sign in from the first address outside the primary data-center range.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Inside the primary data-center range no two-factor authentication is required.
ExpectedResult: 2. Just outside the primary data-center range a two-factor authentication challenge is enforced.

requirement.text: The system SHALL archive vital-sign readings older than 60 days to cold storage and SHALL keep archived readings retrievable within 5 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify readings older than 60 days are archived to a deep archive vault and remain retrievable.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Locate a vital-sign reading dated 90 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect its storage tier and open it.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The reading is reported as held in a deep archive vault.
ExpectedResult: 2. Its values are retrieved and displayed within 5 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify readings newer than 60 days are not archived to a deep archive vault.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Locate a vital-sign reading dated 1 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect its storage tier.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The reading is listed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The reading is in active storage and has not been archived to a deep archive vault.

test_cases.description: Verify the 60-day archival boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Inspect a reading dated exactly 60 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect a reading dated exactly 61 days ago.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 60 days the reading is still in active storage.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 61 days the reading has been archived to a deep archive vault.

requirement.text: The system SHALL let a nurse document a medication administration of Morphine 2 mg, SHALL capture the administration time, and SHALL block a duplicate medication administration within 30 minutes of the previous one for the same medication.

test_cases.description: Verify a nurse can document a medication handoff of Morphine 2 mg.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Morphine 2 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open the Medication Administration Record.
Step: 2. Select the active Morphine 2 mg order and document the administration.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Medication Administration Record is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The medication handoff is documented and Morphine 2 mg is shown as administered.

test_cases.description: Verify a duplicate medication handoff within 30 minutes is blocked.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Morphine 2 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Given Morphine 2 mg was administered 5 minutes ago, select the same order.
Step: 2. Attempt a second administration and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Morphine 2 mg order is selectable.
ExpectedResult: 2. The second administration is blocked citing the duplicate within 30 minutes, and no second record is written.

test_cases.description: Verify the 30-minute duplicate boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Morphine 2 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Attempt a second medication handoff at exactly 30 minutes after the first.
Step: 2. Attempt a second medication handoff at 30 minutes minus 1 second after the first.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At exactly 30 minutes the administration is accepted.
ExpectedResult: 2. Just under 30 minutes the administration is blocked.

test_cases.description: Verify the administration time is captured and persisted.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Morphine 2 mg.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Document a medication handoff and open the recorded entry.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The recorded entry stores the administration time.

requirement.text: The system SHALL deliver a critical lab value notification for calcium to the ordering provider's secure inbox within 5 minutes of result verification.

test_cases.description: Verify a critical lab value notification for calcium is delivered within 5 minutes of verification.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding calcium order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Verify a critical calcium result and record the verification time.
Step: 2. Open the secure inbox and record the notification arrival time.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The critical calcium result is verified.
ExpectedResult: 2. A critical lab value notification is present in the secure inbox and the interval is at or under 5 minutes.

test_cases.description: Verify the 5-minute delivery boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding calcium order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Verify a critical calcium result and measure delivery latency to the secure inbox.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The critical lab value notification is recorded as delivered within 5 minutes of verification.

test_cases.description: Verify the notification routes to the ordering provider specifically.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding calcium order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Verify a critical calcium result ordered by 'dr.t' and inspect the recipient.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The critical lab value notification is routed to the ordering provider's secure inbox, not to any other recipient.

requirement.text: The system SHALL transmit a signed prescription to the selected pharmacy within 180 seconds of signing and SHALL update the order status to 'Sent' upon receiving pharmacy confirmation.

test_cases.description: Verify a signed prescription is transmitted to the selected pharmacy.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Select a medication and destination pharmacy.
Step: 2. Click 'Sign & Send' and observe transmission.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The pharmacy is selected.
ExpectedResult: 2. The signed prescription is transmitted to the selected pharmacy.

test_cases.description: Verify status does not become 'Sent' when the pharmacy is unreachable.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Disable the pharmacy endpoint.
Step: 2. Sign and send a prescription and observe status.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The endpoint is unreachable.
ExpectedResult: 2. Transmission fails, an error is shown, and the status does NOT become 'Sent'.

test_cases.description: Verify transmission occurs within the 180-second limit.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Sign a signed prescription and record the signing time.
Step: 2. Record the arrival time at the pharmacy interface.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The elapsed interval between signing and arrival is at or under 180 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify the order status updates to 'Sent' upon pharmacy confirmation.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Transmit a prescription and have the pharmacy return confirmation.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. On pharmacy confirmation the order status updates to 'Sent'.

requirement.text:
The system SHALL display the ideal body weight computed from height and sex on the patient header, rounded to 1 decimal place(s).

Context: handling of missing or invalid height and sex is specified elsewhere.

test_cases.description: Verify ideal body weight is computed from height and sex and displayed.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; clinician logged in; test patient has recorded height and sex.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient with recorded height and sex.
Step: 2. Inspect the patient header.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The height and sex are shown.
ExpectedResult: 2. The ideal body weight is computed from height and sex and displayed on the patient header.

test_cases.description: Verify the displayed ideal body weight is rounded to 1 decimal place(s).
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; clinician logged in; test patient has recorded height and sex.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Set height and sex to values whose ideal body weight is non-terminating and inspect the header.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The displayed ideal body weight shows no more than 1 decimal place(s).

requirement.text: The system SHALL reject a medication order when the ordered daily dose of Levothyroxine exceeds the formulary maximum daily dose of 300 mcg defined in the formulary, and SHALL display the formulary maximum daily dose in the rejection message.

test_cases.description: Verify a Levothyroxine order within the formulary maximum daily dose is accepted.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Levothyroxine is 300 mcg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> Medications and select Levothyroxine.
Step: 2. Enter a regimen totalling 150 mcg per day.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The medication ordering screen is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The daily total of 150 mcg is calculated and shown.
ExpectedResult: 3. The order is accepted and saved, within the formulary maximum daily dose of 300 mcg.

test_cases.description: Verify a Levothyroxine order exceeding the formulary maximum daily dose is rejected.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Levothyroxine is 300 mcg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> Medications and select Levothyroxine.
Step: 2. Enter a regimen totalling 450 mcg per day.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The medication ordering screen is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The daily total of 450 mcg is calculated and shown.
ExpectedResult: 3. The order is rejected and is not saved.

test_cases.description: Verify the formulary maximum daily dose boundary for Levothyroxine.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Levothyroxine is 300 mcg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Order Levothyroxine totalling exactly 300 mcg per day and sign.
Step: 2. Order Levothyroxine totalling 301 mcg per day and sign.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At exactly 300 mcg the order is accepted, because the dose did not EXCEED the maximum.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 301 mcg the order is rejected.

test_cases.description: Verify the rejection message displays the formulary maximum daily dose value.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; formulary formulary maximum daily dose for Levothyroxine is 300 mcg.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Order Levothyroxine totalling 450 mcg per day and attempt to sign.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The rejection message states the formulary maximum daily dose of 300 mcg.

requirement.text: The system SHALL lock a user account after 5 consecutive failed login attempts within a 10-minute window and SHALL display a lockout notice naming the account and the lockout duration.

test_cases.description: Verify the account locks after 5 consecutive failed logins within 10 minutes.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t510' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit 5 consecutive failed login attempts for 'user.t510' within 10 minutes.
Step: 2. Attempt a further login using the CORRECT password.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. After the 5th consecutive failure the account is locked.
ExpectedResult: 2. Access is denied despite correct credentials and a lockout notice naming the account and lockout duration is shown.

test_cases.description: Verify a successful login before the threshold resets the counter.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t510' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit 4 failed attempts, then log in with the correct password.
Step: 2. Log out and submit 4 further failed attempts.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. After the correct login the failed-attempt counter resets to 0.
ExpectedResult: 2. The account remains unlocked and no lockout notice appears, because no window contains 5 consecutive failures.

test_cases.description: Verify the 5-attempt / 10-minute boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t510' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit exactly 4 failed attempts within 10 minutes and inspect state.
Step: 2. Submit an 5th failed attempt at minute 9 and inspect state.
Step: 3. For a fresh account submit 4 failures, wait past minute 10, then submit one more.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 4 failures the account remains unlocked.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 5 failures within 10 minutes the account locks and the lockout notice appears.
ExpectedResult: 3. The final failure falls outside the 10-minute window, so the account remains unlocked.

requirement.text: The system SHALL automatically end a clinical session after 8 minutes without user input and SHALL require re-authentication before the chart can be accessed again.

test_cases.description: Verify a session ends after 8 minutes of no input and requires re-authentication.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx8' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 8 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient chart and leave the workstation idle for 8 minutes.
Step: 2. Attempt to scroll the chart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 8 minutes of inactivity the session ends and the chart is hidden.
ExpectedResult: 2. The chart is inaccessible and a re-authentication prompt is displayed; access is restored only after valid credentials.

test_cases.description: Verify input before the timeout keeps the session active.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx8' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 8 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Remain idle for 7 minutes, then click within the chart.
Step: 2. Remain idle for a further 7 minutes, then click within the chart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The session remains active and no prompt appears.
ExpectedResult: 2. The session remains active because each input resets the inactivity timer.

test_cases.description: Verify the 8-minute inactivity boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx8' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 8 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Remain idle for exactly 8 minutes minus 1 second; inspect state.
Step: 2. Allow inactivity to reach exactly 8 minutes 0 seconds; inspect state.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Just under 8 minutes the session is still active.
ExpectedResult: 2. At exactly 8 minutes the session ends and re-authentication is required.

requirement.text: The system SHALL alert the ordering provider when two active medications (Fluoxetine and Tramadol) have a known major drug-drug interaction, and the alert SHALL name both interacting medications.

test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Fluoxetine is shown as active.
ExpectedResult: 2. A major drug-drug interaction alert is presented and the alert text names both Fluoxetine and Tramadol.

test_cases.description: Verify the drug-drug interaction alert text names both interacting medications.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; interaction database classifies Fluoxetine + Tramadol as a major interaction.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Trigger the Fluoxetine + Tramadol interaction and inspect the alert text.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The alert text explicitly contains both 'Fluoxetine' and 'Tramadol' by name.

requirement.text: The system SHALL restrict access to adoption records to users holding the Social Work role and SHALL deny access to all other roles, recording each denied attempt in the audit log.

test_cases.description: Verify a Social Work role holder can open a adoption records record.

ExpectedResult: 1. The Social Work role is active.

test_cases.expectedResults:

requirement.text: The system SHALL calculate a Ceftriaxone dose as 50 milligrams per kilogram of the patient's recorded body weight and SHALL round the calculated dose to 1 decimal place(s).

test_cases.description: Verify the Ceftriaxone dose is calculated as 50 mg/kg of charted body height.

requirement.text: The system SHALL require a documented override reason of at least 12 characters when a provider dismisses a high-severity allergy alert, and SHALL store the override reason with the order.

ExpectedResult: 1. The high-severity allergy alert is presented and a override reason field is shown.
ExpectedResult: 2. The override is accepted and the order is signed.

test_cases.description: Verify the alert cannot be dismissed with no override reason.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient triggers a high-severity allergy alert.

ExpectedResult: 1. A override reason field is shown.

test_cases.steps:

test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The stored order detail shows the exact override reason text that was entered.

requirement.text: The system SHALL reject a new patient registration when the supplied medical record number (MRN-J) already exists in the system, and SHALL display the conflicting medical record number in the rejection message.

test_cases.description: Verify a new patient can be registered with a unique medical record number.

test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open Patient Registration -> New Patient.
Step: 2. Enter demographics with a unique medical record number 'MRN-J-0001'.
Step: 3. Click 'Register'.
test_cases.expectedResults:

test_cases.description: Verify registration is rejected when the medical record number already exists.

requirement.text: The system SHALL trigger a sepsis alert when a patient's creatinine exceeds 2 mg/dL AND the patient's potassium exceeds 5 mmol/L within the same 12-hour window.

test_cases.description: Verify a sepsis alert triggers when both creatinine and potassium exceed thresholds within 12 hours.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record creatinine of 4 mg/dL at 09:00.
Step: 2. Record potassium of 7 mmol/L within the same 12-hour window.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The creatinine is recorded.
ExpectedResult: 2. A sepsis alert is triggered and displayed for the patient.

test_cases.description: Verify no sepsis alert triggers when neither value exceeds its threshold.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record creatinine of -3 mg/dL.
Step: 2. Record potassium of 3 mmol/L.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Both values are recorded below threshold.
ExpectedResult: 2. No sepsis alert is triggered.

test_cases.description: Verify no sepsis alert triggers when only one factor exceeds its threshold.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record only creatinine above 2 mg/dL (with potassium normal).
Step: 2. Separately record only potassium above 5 mmol/L (with creatinine normal).
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. With only creatinine elevated, no sepsis alert triggers.
ExpectedResult: 2. With only potassium elevated, no sepsis alert triggers.

requirement.text: The system SHALL allow a provider to place a electrophysiology order, SHALL allow selection of a collection priority of STAT or Routine, and SHALL print a specimen label containing the patient's MRN and the electrophysiology order ID.

test_cases.description: Verify a provider can place a electrophysiology order with STAT priority.

test_cases.expectedResults:

ExpectedResult: 3. The specimen label wording matches the requirement exactly.

test_cases.description: Verify the order cannot be signed without a collection priority.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test patient chart open.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> electrophysiology and select a test.
Step: 2. Leave the collection priority unselected.
Step: 3. Click 'Sign & Send'.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. A test is selectable.
ExpectedResult: 2. The order is rejected with a message requiring a priority of STAT or Routine, and no order is created.

test_cases.description: Verify Routine priority and the specimen label content.

test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The order is created with priority Routine.
ExpectedResult: 2. The specimen label contains the patient's MRN and the electrophysiology order ID.

requirement.text:
The system SHALL display a 'Airborne Precautions' banner on the patient header when the patient has an active airborne-isolation order.

requirement.text: The system SHALL require two-factor authentication for any user signing in from an IP address outside the branch-clinic VPN range, and SHALL grant access only after a valid second factor is supplied.

test_cases.description: Verify an invalid second factor denies access.

Step: 1. From an IP outside the branch-clinic VPN range, enter valid credentials.
Step: 2. Enter an INVALID second factor code.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. A two-factor authentication challenge is presented.
ExpectedResult: 2. The invalid second factor is rejected and access is denied.

test_cases.description: Verify the the branch-clinic VPN range boundary is enforced at the edge of the range.

test_cases.expectedResults:

ExpectedResult: 2. Just outside the branch-clinic VPN range a two-factor authentication challenge is enforced.

requirement.text: The system SHALL archive vital-sign readings older than 60 days to cold storage and SHALL keep archived readings retrievable within 10 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify readings older than 60 days are archived to cold storage and remain retrievable.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Locate a vital-sign reading dated 90 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect its storage tier and open it.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The reading is reported as held in cold storage.
ExpectedResult: 2. Its values are retrieved and displayed within 10 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify readings newer than 60 days are not archived to cold storage.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Locate a vital-sign reading dated 1 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect its storage tier.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The reading is listed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The reading is in active storage and has not been archived to cold storage.

test_cases.description: Verify the 60-day archival boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Inspect a reading dated exactly 60 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect a reading dated exactly 61 days ago.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 60 days the reading is still in active storage.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 61 days the reading has been archived to cold storage.

requirement.text: The system SHALL let a nurse document a medication administration of Insulin lispro 4 units, SHALL capture the administration time, and SHALL block a duplicate medication administration within 30 minutes of the previous one for the same medication.

test_cases.description: Verify a duplicate medication administration within 30 minutes is blocked.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Insulin lispro 4 units.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Given Insulin lispro 4 units was administered 5 minutes ago, select the same order.
Step: 2. Attempt a second administration and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Insulin lispro 4 units order is selectable.
ExpectedResult: 2. The second administration is blocked citing the duplicate within 30 minutes, and no second record is written.

test_cases.description: Verify the 30-minute duplicate boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Insulin lispro 4 units.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Attempt a second medication administration at exactly 30 minutes after the first.
Step: 2. Attempt a second medication administration at 30 minutes minus 1 second after the first.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At exactly 30 minutes the administration is accepted.
ExpectedResult: 2. Just under 30 minutes the administration is blocked.

test_cases.description: Verify the administration time is captured and persisted.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Insulin lispro 4 units.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Document a medication administration and open the recorded entry.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The recorded entry stores the administration time.

requirement.text: The system SHALL deliver a critical lab value notification for potassium to the ordering provider's secure inbox within 10 minutes of result verification.

test_cases.description: Verify a critical lab value notification for potassium is delivered within 10 minutes of verification.

test_cases.steps:

test_cases.expectedResults:

test_cases.description: Verify duplicate verification events do not create a second notification.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding potassium order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Emit the same verified potassium result twice.
Step: 2. Inspect the secure inbox.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The result is verified twice.
ExpectedResult: 2. Exactly one critical lab value notification is present in the secure inbox; the duplicate is suppressed.

test_cases.description: Verify the 10-minute delivery boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding potassium order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Verify a critical potassium result and measure delivery latency to the secure inbox.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The critical lab value notification is recorded as delivered within 10 minutes of verification.

test_cases.description: Verify the notification routes to the ordering provider specifically.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding potassium order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Verify a critical potassium result ordered by 'dr.t' and inspect the recipient.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The critical lab value notification is routed to the ordering provider's secure inbox, not to any other recipient.

requirement.text: The system SHALL transmit a signed prescription to the selected pharmacy within 300 seconds of signing and SHALL update the order status to 'Sent' upon receiving pharmacy confirmation.

test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The endpoint is unreachable.

test_cases.description: Verify transmission occurs within the 300-second limit.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Sign a signed prescription and record the signing time.
Step: 2. Record the arrival time at the pharmacy interface.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The elapsed interval between signing and arrival is at or under 300 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify the order status updates to 'Sent' upon pharmacy confirmation.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Transmit a prescription and have the pharmacy return confirmation.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. On pharmacy confirmation the order status updates to 'Sent'.

requirement.text:

requirement.text: The system SHALL reject a medication order when the ordered daily dose of Warfarin exceeds the formulary maximum daily dose of 10 mg defined in the formulary, and SHALL display the formulary maximum daily dose in the rejection message.

test_cases.description: Verify a Warfarin order within the formulary maximum daily dose is accepted.

test_cases.description: Verify a Warfarin order exceeding the formulary maximum daily dose is rejected.

Step: 1. Navigate to Orders -> Medications and select Warfarin.

test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The rejection message states the formulary maximum daily dose of 10 mg.

requirement.text: The system SHALL lock a user account after 5 consecutive failed login attempts within a 15-minute window and SHALL display a lockout notice naming the account and the lockout duration.

test_cases.description: Verify the account locks after 5 consecutive failed logins within 15 minutes.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t515' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit 5 consecutive failed login attempts for 'user.t515' within 15 minutes.
Step: 2. Attempt a further login using the CORRECT password.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. After the 5th consecutive failure the account is locked.
ExpectedResult: 2. Access is denied despite correct credentials and a lockout notice naming the account and lockout duration is shown.

test_cases.description: Verify the 5-attempt / 15-minute boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test account 'user.t515' active and unlocked; system clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Submit exactly 4 failed attempts within 15 minutes and inspect state.
Step: 2. Submit an 5th failed attempt at minute 14 and inspect state.
Step: 3. For a fresh account submit 4 failures, wait past minute 15, then submit one more.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 4 failures the account remains unlocked.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 5 failures within 15 minutes the account locks and the lockout notice appears.
ExpectedResult: 3. The final failure falls outside the 15-minute window, so the account remains unlocked.

requirement.text: The system SHALL automatically end a clinical session after 12 minutes without user input and SHALL require re-authentication before the chart can be accessed again.

test_cases.description: Verify a session ends after 12 minutes of no input and requires re-authentication.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx12' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 12 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient chart and leave the workstation idle for 12 minutes.
Step: 2. Attempt to scroll the chart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 12 minutes of inactivity the session ends and the chart is hidden.
ExpectedResult: 2. The chart is inaccessible and a re-authentication prompt is displayed; access is restored only after valid credentials.

test_cases.description: Verify input before the timeout keeps the session active.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx12' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 12 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Remain idle for 11 minutes, then click within the chart.
Step: 2. Remain idle for a further 11 minutes, then click within the chart.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The session remains active and no prompt appears.
ExpectedResult: 2. The session remains active because each input resets the inactivity timer.

test_cases.description: Verify the 12-minute inactivity boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.sx12' logged in with a patient chart open; session timeout 12 minutes; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Remain idle for exactly 12 minutes minus 1 second; inspect state.
Step: 2. Allow inactivity to reach exactly 12 minutes 0 seconds; inspect state.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Just under 12 minutes the session is still active.
ExpectedResult: 2. At exactly 12 minutes the session ends and re-authentication is required.

requirement.text: The system SHALL alert the ordering provider when two active medications (Verapamil and Metoprolol) have a known major drug-drug interaction, and the alert SHALL name both interacting medications.

test_cases.description: Verify no alert is raised for a non-interacting pair.

Step: 1. Confirm the patient has an active medication with no known interaction with the ordered drug.
Step: 2. Order and sign a non-interacting medication.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The prior medication is active.
ExpectedResult: 2. The order is signed with no drug-drug interaction alert presented.

test_cases.description: Verify the drug-drug interaction alert text names both interacting medications.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; interaction database classifies Verapamil + Metoprolol as a major interaction.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Trigger the Verapamil + Metoprolol interaction and inspect the alert text.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The alert text explicitly contains both 'Verapamil' and 'Metoprolol' by name.

requirement.text: The system SHALL restrict access to minor confidential records to users holding the Pediatric Confidential role and SHALL deny access to all other roles, recording each denied attempt in the audit log.

test_cases.description: Verify a user without the Pediatric Confidential role is denied access.

Step: 2. Attempt to open the minor confidential records.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Login succeeds without the Pediatric Confidential role.
ExpectedResult: 2. Access is denied and no minor confidential records content is displayed.

test_cases.description: Verify each denied attempt is recorded in the audit log.

test_cases.steps:

Step: 2. As an auditor query the audit log for denials.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Access is denied.
ExpectedResult: 2. An audit entry recording the denied attempt is present.

requirement.text: The system SHALL calculate a Clindamycin dose as 8 milligrams per kilogram of the patient's recorded body weight and SHALL round the calculated dose to 1 decimal place(s).

test_cases.description: Verify the Clindamycin dose is calculated as 8 mg/kg of recorded body weight.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; pediatric patient with a recorded body weight; Clindamycin dosing is 8 mg/kg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Confirm the recorded body weight is 12.0 kg.
Step: 2. Select weight-based Clindamycin dosing at 8 mg/kg.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The recorded body weight of 12.0 kg is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The system calculates and displays a dose of 96.0 mg.

test_cases.description: Verify calculation is blocked when no recorded body weight is recorded.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; pediatric patient with a recorded body weight; Clindamycin dosing is 8 mg/kg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open a patient with NO recorded body weight.
Step: 2. Select weight-based Clindamycin dosing at 8 mg/kg.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The chart shows no recorded body weight.
ExpectedResult: 2. No dose is calculated; an error states a recorded weight is required and the order cannot be signed.

requirement.text: The system SHALL require a documented override reason of at least 12 characters when a provider dismisses a hard-stop dosing alert, and SHALL store the override reason with the order.

test_cases.description: Verify a hard-stop dosing alert can be dismissed with a sufficient override reason.

test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Dismiss the hard-stop dosing alert with a valid override reason and open the signed order detail.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The stored order detail shows the exact override reason text that was entered.

requirement.text: The system SHALL reject a new patient registration when the supplied medical record number (MRN-K) already exists in the system, and SHALL display the conflicting medical record number in the rejection message.

requirement.text: The system SHALL trigger a sepsis alert when a patient's heart rate exceeds 130 bpm AND the patient's systolic blood pressure exceeds 90 mmHg within the same 2-hour window.

test_cases.description: Verify a sepsis alert triggers when both heart rate and systolic blood pressure exceed thresholds within 2 hours.

test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record heart rate of 158 bpm at 09:00.

test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The heart rate is recorded.

test_cases.description: Verify no sepsis alert triggers when neither value exceeds its threshold.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; test patient admitted; vitals entry available.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Record heart rate of 125 bpm.
Step: 2. Record systolic blood pressure of 88 mmHg.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. Both values are recorded below threshold.
ExpectedResult: 2. No sepsis alert is triggered.

test_cases.description: Verify the exact thresholds and the 2-hour window boundary.

ExpectedResult: 2. With only systolic blood pressure elevated, no sepsis alert triggers.

requirement.text:
The system SHALL display a 'Droplet Precautions' banner on the patient header when the patient has an active droplet-isolation order.

test_cases.description: Verify the 'Droplet Precautions' banner appears for a patient with an active droplet-isolation order.

requirement.text: The system SHALL require two-factor authentication for any user signing in from an IP address outside the telehealth gateway range, and SHALL grant access only after a valid second factor is supplied.

test_cases.description: Verify two-factor authentication is required and grants access from an external IP.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'dr.ext' enrolled in two-factor authentication; workstation IP outside the telehealth gateway range.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. From an IP outside the telehealth gateway range, enter valid credentials.
Step: 2. Enter a valid second factor code.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The source IP is recognised as outside the telehealth gateway range and a two-factor authentication challenge is presented.
ExpectedResult: 2. The valid second factor is accepted and access is granted.

test_cases.description: Verify an invalid second factor denies access.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; user 'dr.ext' enrolled in two-factor authentication; workstation IP outside the telehealth gateway range.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. From an IP outside the telehealth gateway range, enter valid credentials.
Step: 2. Enter an INVALID second factor code.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. A two-factor authentication challenge is presented.
ExpectedResult: 2. The invalid second factor is rejected and access is denied.

requirement.text: The system SHALL archive vital-sign readings older than 90 days to cold storage and SHALL keep archived readings retrievable within 2 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify readings older than 90 days are archived to cold storage and remain retrievable.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Locate a vital-sign reading dated 120 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect its storage tier and open it.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The reading is reported as held in cold storage.
ExpectedResult: 2. Its values are retrieved and displayed within 2 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify the 90-day archival boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; archive viewer accessible; clock controllable.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Inspect a reading dated exactly 90 days ago.
Step: 2. Inspect a reading dated exactly 91 days ago.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At 90 days the reading is still in active storage.
ExpectedResult: 2. At 91 days the reading has been archived to cold storage.

requirement.text: The system SHALL let a nurse document a medication administration of Furosemide 40 mg, SHALL capture the administration time, and SHALL block a duplicate medication administration within 30 minutes of the previous one for the same medication.

test_cases.description: Verify a nurse can document a medication administration of Furosemide 40 mg.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Furosemide 40 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Open the Medication Administration Record.
Step: 2. Select the active Furosemide 40 mg order and document the administration.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Medication Administration Record is displayed.
ExpectedResult: 2. The medication administration is documented and Furosemide 40 mg is shown as administered.

test_cases.description: Verify a duplicate medication administration within 30 minutes is blocked.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Furosemide 40 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Given Furosemide 40 mg was administered 5 minutes ago, select the same order.
Step: 2. Attempt a second administration and confirm.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The Furosemide 40 mg order is selectable.
ExpectedResult: 2. The second administration is blocked citing the duplicate within 30 minutes, and no second record is written.

test_cases.description: Verify the 30-minute duplicate boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Furosemide 40 mg.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Attempt a second medication administration at exactly 30 minutes after the first.
Step: 2. Attempt a second medication administration at 30 minutes minus 1 second after the first.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. At exactly 30 minutes the administration is accepted.
ExpectedResult: 2. Just under 30 minutes the administration is blocked.

test_cases.description: Verify the administration time is captured and persisted.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; nurse 'nurse.t' logged in; test patient has an active order for Furosemide 40 mg.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Document a medication administration and open the recorded entry.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The recorded entry stores the administration time.

requirement.text: The system SHALL deliver a critical lab value notification for troponin to the ordering provider's secure inbox within 10 minutes of result verification.

test_cases.description: Verify a critical lab value notification for troponin is delivered within 10 minutes of verification.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding troponin order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Verify a critical troponin result and record the verification time.
Step: 2. Open the secure inbox and record the notification arrival time.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The critical troponin result is verified.
ExpectedResult: 2. A critical lab value notification is present in the secure inbox and the interval is at or under 10 minutes.

test_cases.description: Verify the 10-minute delivery boundary.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding troponin order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Verify a critical troponin result and measure delivery latency to the secure inbox.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The critical lab value notification is recorded as delivered within 10 minutes of verification.

test_cases.description: Verify the notification routes to the ordering provider specifically.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider 'dr.t' has an outstanding troponin order; secure inbox accessible.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Verify a critical troponin result ordered by 'dr.t' and inspect the recipient.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The critical lab value notification is routed to the ordering provider's secure inbox, not to any other recipient.

requirement.text: The system SHALL transmit a signed prescription to the selected pharmacy within 240 seconds of signing and SHALL update the order status to 'Sent' upon receiving pharmacy confirmation.

test_cases.description: Verify a signed prescription is transmitted to the selected pharmacy.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Select a medication and destination pharmacy.
Step: 2. Click 'Sign & Send' and observe transmission.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The pharmacy is selected.
ExpectedResult: 2. The signed prescription is transmitted to the selected pharmacy.

test_cases.description: Verify status does not become 'Sent' when the pharmacy is unreachable.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Disable the pharmacy endpoint.
Step: 2. Sign and send a prescription and observe status.
test_cases.expectedResults:
ExpectedResult: 1. The endpoint is unreachable.
ExpectedResult: 2. Transmission fails, an error is shown, and the status does NOT become 'Sent'.

test_cases.description: Verify transmission occurs within the 240-second limit.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps:
Step: 1. Sign a signed prescription and record the signing time.
Step: 2. Record the arrival time at the pharmacy interface.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. The elapsed interval between signing and arrival is at or under 240 seconds.

test_cases.description: Verify the order status updates to 'Sent' upon pharmacy confirmation.
test_cases.setup: HealthCore EHR test environment; provider logged in; test pharmacy 'Riverside #2' configured to confirm receipt.
test_cases.steps: Step: 1. Transmit a prescription and have the pharmacy return confirmation.
test_cases.expectedResults: ExpectedResult: 1. On pharmacy confirmation the order status updates to 'Sent'.

requirement.text:

test_cases.expectedResults:
